objects.description: Function pointer type for client-supplied memory allocation. Implementations should allocate sz bytes and may use ctx as a user context. Returns pointer to allocated memory or NULL on failure.
Function pointer type for client-supplied deallocation. Frees memory previously allocated by the paired allocator/reallocator. ctx is a user context pointer.

objects.definition: typedef void * (*yajl_realloc_func)(void *ctx, void * ptr, unsigned int sz);
objects.description: Function pointer type for client-supplied reallocation. Resizes a prior allocation ptr to sz bytes, using ctx as context. Returns new pointer or NULL on failure (original pointer handling follows realloc semantics as implemented by the provider).

Configuration structure bundling client-provided memory management callbacks and a shared context pointer. Pass to YAJL allocation APIs to override default memory routines. All fields should be set consistently; ctx is passed to each callback.
Enumeration of parser status/error codes returned by YAJL parsing APIs. Covers success, client-canceled, need-more-data, generic parse error, and allocation failure.
Opaque handle type for a YAJL JSON parser instance. The underlying struct is not defined in this header; treat it as an opaque resource managed by the YAJL allocation and free functions.

Callback vtable passed to the parser. Function pointers are invoked on parsing events (null, boolean, numbers, strings, maps, arrays). Returning non-zero continues parsing; zero cancels with yajl_status_client_canceled. If yajl_number is non-NULL it is used for all numbers; otherwise integer/double are used with range limits as noted.
Configuration structure for the parser. Controls allowance of JavaScript-style comments and enforcement of valid UTF-8 in strings.
Enumeration of status and error codes returned by YAJL generator APIs, covering normal completion, misuse, invalid numbers, depth issues, buffer state, and allocation failure.
Opaque handle type for a YAJL JSON generator instance. The underlying struct is not defined in this header; handle is created by allocator functions and freed by yajl_gen_free.
Function pointer type for generator output callbacks. Implementations receive a context pointer, a character buffer, and its length.
Configuration struct for YAJL generator controlling pretty-printing (beautify), custom indent string, and HTML-safe escaping of '/'. Populate and pass to allocator functions; storage is caller-owned.

No custom data types are defined in this header. The only symbol is a function declaration for yajl_version returning an int. Macros YAJL_MAJOR, YAJL_MINOR, YAJL_MICRO, and YAJL_VERSION are version constants. Since no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes are defined here, there is no applicable object type to document.

functions.name: yajl_status_to_string
functions.signature: YAJL_API const char * yajl_status_to_string(yajl_status code);
functions.description: Return a human-readable English string describing a YAJL status/error code. Useful for logging or diagnostics when interpreting yajl_status values returned by other API calls. Lifetime/ownership of the returned string is not specified in this header (unknown).
requirements: code must be a valid value of the yajl_status enum

functions.name: yajl_alloc
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_handle yajl_alloc(const yajl_callbacks * callbacks, const yajl_parser_config * config, const yajl_alloc_funcs * allocFuncs, void * ctx);
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a YAJL JSON parser handle. You may provide callbacks to receive parse events, parser configuration, custom allocation functions, and an opaque context pointer passed to each callback. If callbacks is NULL, the handle can still be used for validation-only parsing.
requirements: callbacks may be NULL for validation-only parsing (as stated)

If callbacks is non-NULL, each function pointer supplied must match the declared signatures and must return non-zero to continue parsing; returning zero will cancel the parse and cause yajl_status_client_canceled
ctx is an opaque pointer and will be passed back to callbacks as given
The returned handle must later be released with yajl_free
config should point to a valid yajl_parser_config if provided; semantics: allowComments enables C/JavaScript-style comments; checkUTF8 makes invalid UTF-8 a parse error
Strings delivered to yajl_string and yajl_map_key callbacks are not NUL-terminated and are valid for the duration implied by the parser (as per comments)
Number-handling behavior depends on which number callbacks are provided (see comments in header)

functions.name: yajl_reset_parser
functions.signature: YAJL_API void yajl_reset_parser(yajl_handle hand);
functions.description: Reset the parser’s lexer so the handle can be reused for a new stream without reallocating a new parser. Intended to clear internal state between parsing sessions on the same handle.
requirements: hand must be a valid parser handle previously returned by yajl_alloc and not yet freed

functions.name: yajl_free
functions.signature: YAJL_API void yajl_free(yajl_handle handle);
functions.description: Free a YAJL parser handle previously allocated with yajl_alloc, releasing all associated resources.
requirements: handle must be a valid yajl_handle obtained from yajl_alloc
After calling, the handle must not be used again

functions.name: yajl_parse
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_status yajl_parse(yajl_handle hand, const unsigned char * jsonText, unsigned int jsonTextLength);
functions.description: Incrementally parse a chunk of UTF-8 JSON text. Triggers callbacks as JSON entities are recognized. Supports streaming: call repeatedly with successive buffers; if insufficient data is detected, the function returns yajl_status_insufficient_data and you should supply more input. Use with yajl_parse_complete at end-of-input.
requirements: hand must be a valid parser handle from yajl_alloc
jsonText must point to a buffer of at least jsonTextLength bytes
jsonText must contain UTF-8 JSON text; if checkUTF8 was enabled in the config, invalid UTF-8 will cause a parse error
Caller must check the returned yajl_status and react accordingly (ok, client_canceled, insufficient_data, error, alloc_failed)
When callbacks are provided, they may be invoked during the call; if any callback returns 0 the parse stops and yajl_status_client_canceled is returned
For stream parsing, the caller may provide partial tokens; on yajl_status_insufficient_data provide more input and call again

functions.name: yajl_parse_complete
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_status yajl_parse_complete(yajl_handle hand);
functions.description: Signal end-of-input and ask YAJL to resolve any buffered state. Useful in streaming scenarios where the last chunk might leave the parser undecided (e.g., a trailing digit).
requirements: hand must be a valid parser handle from yajl_alloc
Should be called after the final yajl_parse call for a stream to flush remaining buffered content
Caller must check the returned yajl_status for success or error

functions.name: yajl_get_error
functions.signature: YAJL_API unsigned char * yajl_get_error(yajl_handle hand, int verbose, const unsigned char * jsonText, unsigned int jsonTextLength);
functions.description: Return a dynamically allocated, human-readable error message describing the parser’s current error state. If verbose is non-zero, the message will include a snippet of the provided JSON text with an arrow pointing to the error location. The returned string must be freed with yajl_free_error.
requirements: hand must be a valid parser handle from yajl_alloc
The returned pointer must be freed with yajl_free_error using the same hand
verbose: if non-zero, include contextual JSON text in the message
jsonText/jsonTextLength should describe the relevant input buffer to contextualize the error when verbose is non-zero
Do not use or free the returned buffer except via yajl_free_error

functions.name: yajl_get_bytes_consumed
functions.signature: YAJL_API unsigned int yajl_get_bytes_consumed(yajl_handle hand);
functions.description: Report the number of bytes consumed from the most recent input chunk passed to yajl_parse. On error, this gives the offset within the last chunk where the error occurred; on success, it can be used to detect unconsumed trailing data.
requirements: hand must be a valid parser handle from yajl_alloc
Should be called after at least one call to yajl_parse to have meaningful data

functions.name: yajl_free_error
functions.signature: YAJL_API void yajl_free_error(yajl_handle hand, unsigned char * str);
functions.description: Free an error message buffer previously allocated by yajl_get_error for the given handle.
requirements: hand must be the same parser handle used to obtain str via yajl_get_error
str must be a pointer returned by yajl_get_error and not already freed
After freeing, str must not be used

functions.name: yajl_gen_alloc
functions.signature:
YAJL_API yajl_gen yajl_gen_alloc(const yajl_gen_config * config,
                                     const yajl_alloc_funcs * allocFuncs);
functions.description: Allocate and initialize a YAJL JSON generator that stores output in an internal buffer. Configure behavior (beautify, indent string, HTML-safe escaping) via the provided config; optionally supply custom memory allocators. Returns a generator handle on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: config must point to a valid yajl_gen_config structure initialized by the caller.
allocFuncs may be NULL; if NULL, malloc/free/realloc are used.
On success, the returned yajl_gen handle must be freed with yajl_gen_free.
Callers should check the return value for NULL to detect allocation or parameter errors.
If beautify is enabled in config, indentString controls indentation; otherwise indentString is ignored.
Thread-safety is not implied; do not share a single generator across threads without external synchronization.

functions.name: yajl_gen_alloc2
functions.description: Allocate a YAJL JSON generator that can either print output via a user-supplied callback or store it in an internal buffer when callback is NULL. Allows configuring formatting and custom allocators. Returns a generator handle on success or NULL on failure.
requirements: callback may be NULL; when NULL, output is stored in an internal buffer accessible via yajl_gen_get_buf.

If callback is non-NULL, it must have the signature void (*)(void *ctx, const char *str, unsigned int len) and be safe to call repeatedly with contiguous JSON output chunks; it must not assume NUL termination of str.
ctx is an opaque pointer passed back to callback; it may be NULL.
config must point to a valid yajl_gen_config structure initialized by the caller.
allocFuncs may be NULL; if NULL, malloc/free/realloc are used.
On success, the returned yajl_gen handle must be freed with yajl_gen_free.
Callers should check the return value for NULL to detect allocation or parameter errors.
When a print callback is provided, yajl_gen_get_buf will not be usable and will return yajl_gen_no_buf.

functions.name: yajl_gen_free
functions.signature: YAJL_API void yajl_gen_free(yajl_gen handle);
functions.description: Release all resources associated with a YAJL JSON generator created by yajl_gen_alloc or yajl_gen_alloc2.
requirements: handle must be a valid yajl_gen previously returned by yajl_gen_alloc or yajl_gen_alloc2.
After this call, handle is invalid and must not be used.
It is safe to pass a generator that has generated partial or complete JSON; internal state will be freed.
Do not call twice on the same handle (use-after-free).

functions.name: yajl_gen_integer
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_gen_status yajl_gen_integer(yajl_gen hand, long int number);
functions.description: Append a JSON integer value to the current output context of the generator.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen in a non-error state.
number must be representable as a JSON integer literal (C long int will be rendered as digits).
Must be called in a position where a JSON value is valid (e.g., as an array element or as a map value).
When inside a map and expecting a key, only yajl_gen_string is valid; calling this there will yield yajl_gen_keys_must_be_strings.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors (e.g., generation complete, depth errors, or in-error-state).

functions.name: yajl_gen_double
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_gen_status yajl_gen_double(yajl_gen hand, double number);
functions.description: Append a JSON floating-point number to the current output context. Returns yajl_gen_invalid_number if the value is NaN or infinity, which are not representable in JSON.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen in a non-error state.
number must not be NaN or infinity; otherwise the function returns yajl_gen_invalid_number and no output is generated.
Must be called where a JSON value is valid (array element or map value, not a map key).
When inside a map and expecting a key, only yajl_gen_string is valid; calling this there will yield yajl_gen_keys_must_be_strings.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors.

functions.name: yajl_gen_long
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_gen_status yajl_gen_long(yajl_gen hand, long value);
functions.description: Append a JSON integer value from a C long to the current output context.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen in a non-error state.
Must be called in a position where a JSON value is valid (array element or map value).
When inside a map and expecting a key, only yajl_gen_string is valid; calling this there will yield yajl_gen_keys_must_be_strings.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors.

functions.name: yajl_gen_number
functions.description: Append a JSON number literal from a caller-supplied character buffer. This allows emitting numbers that may not fit native types (e.g., big integers or precise decimals).
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen in a non-error state.
num must point to a readable buffer of length len containing a syntactically valid JSON number literal (no surrounding quotes).
The buffer does not need to be NUL-terminated; len specifies the exact length.
Must be called where a JSON value is valid (array element or map value).
When inside a map and expecting a key, only yajl_gen_string is valid; calling this there will yield yajl_gen_keys_must_be_strings.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors.

functions.name: yajl_gen_string
functions.description: Append a JSON string value from a caller-supplied byte buffer. Used both for string values and for object keys when inside a map.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen in a non-error state.
str must point to a readable buffer of length len; the buffer need not be NUL-terminated.
When generating map keys, this function must be used; other value functions used at a key position will cause yajl_gen_keys_must_be_strings.
The buffer contents will be JSON-escaped as needed (including optional HTML-safe escaping if configured).
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors.

functions.name: yajl_gen_null
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_gen_status yajl_gen_null(yajl_gen hand);
functions.description: Append the JSON literal null to the current output context.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen in a non-error state.
Must be called where a JSON value is valid (array element or map value).
When inside a map and expecting a key, only yajl_gen_string is valid; calling this there will yield yajl_gen_keys_must_be_strings.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors.

functions.name: yajl_gen_bool
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_gen_status yajl_gen_bool(yajl_gen hand, int boolean);
functions.description: Append a JSON boolean value (true or false) to the current output context based on the provided integer.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen in a non-error state.
boolean is interpreted in C style (0 is false; non-zero is true).
Must be called where a JSON value is valid (array element or map value).
When inside a map and expecting a key, only yajl_gen_string is valid; calling this there will yield yajl_gen_keys_must_be_strings.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors.

functions.name: yajl_gen_map_open
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_gen_status yajl_gen_map_open(yajl_gen hand);
functions.description: Begin a JSON object (map) by emitting '{' and entering key/value generation state.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen in a non-error state.
Subsequent entries must alternate between string keys (via yajl_gen_string) and values, following JSON object rules.
Each yajl_gen_map_open must be matched with a corresponding yajl_gen_map_close; otherwise depth/state errors may occur.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors, including depth overflow (yajl_max_depth_exceeded).

functions.name: yajl_gen_map_close
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_gen_status yajl_gen_map_close(yajl_gen hand);
functions.description: Close the current JSON object by emitting '}' and exiting map state.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen currently inside an open map.
Must not be called more times than corresponding yajl_gen_map_open calls; otherwise yajl_depth_underflow may occur.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors.

functions.name: yajl_gen_array_open
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_gen_status yajl_gen_array_open(yajl_gen hand);
functions.description: Begin a JSON array by emitting '[' and entering array element generation state.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen in a non-error state.
Each yajl_gen_array_open must be matched with a corresponding yajl_gen_array_close.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors, including depth overflow (yajl_max_depth_exceeded).

functions.name: yajl_gen_array_close
functions.signature: YAJL_API yajl_gen_status yajl_gen_array_close(yajl_gen hand);
functions.description: Close the current JSON array by emitting ']' and exiting array state.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen currently inside an open array.
Must not be called more times than corresponding yajl_gen_array_open calls; otherwise yajl_depth_underflow may occur.
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors.

functions.name: yajl_gen_get_buf
functions.description: Access the generator’s internal, NUL-terminated output buffer and its current length. Intended for incremental output; call yajl_gen_clear afterward to reuse the buffer for continued generation.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen configured without a print callback; if a callback was provided at allocation time, this will return yajl_gen_no_buf.
buf must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the address of the internal buffer; the pointed-to data is owned by the generator and must not be freed or modified by the caller.
len must be a non-NULL pointer to receive the current buffer length in bytes (not including the terminating NUL).
Caller must check the returned yajl_gen_status and handle errors.
For streaming use, call yajl_gen_clear after consuming the buffer to continue generating; otherwise data will accumulate.
Do not assume the buffer pointer remains valid across calls that mutate the generator state (e.g., further generation or clear).

functions.name: yajl_gen_clear
functions.signature: YAJL_API void yajl_gen_clear(yajl_gen hand);
functions.description: Clear the generator’s output buffer while preserving internal generation state. Enables incremental (streaming) JSON output without resetting the open/close state of arrays or objects.
requirements: hand must be a valid yajl_gen.
This does not reset generator state; do not call it to terminate or balance structures—only to discard the accumulated output buffer.
After clearing, previously obtained buffer pointers from yajl_gen_get_buf become invalid.
Safe to call multiple times between output retrievals.

functions.name: yajl_version
functions.signature: extern int YAJL_API yajl_version(void);
functions.description: Returns the YAJL library version as an integer encoded in the same format as the YAJL_VERSION macro ((YAJL_MAJOR * 10000) + (YAJL_MINOR * 100) + YAJL_MICRO). Typical usage is to query the runtime library version and optionally compare it against the compile-time YAJL_VERSION to detect mismatches. No parameters and no side effects are expected.
requirements: No arguments must be provided.
May be called without prior initialization of the library.
Caller should be prepared to handle any non-negative integer consistent with the (major*10000 + minor*100 + micro) encoding indicated by the header macros.
Function is declared with YAJL_API; ensure correct linkage/visibility when linking against the YAJL library.

data_types.description: Text buffer containing JSON encoded data in UTF-8. May be complete or partial fragments when used for streaming parse contexts. Can include any JSON value: objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, or null. When used for verbose error context, it is the original JSON input bytes.

A raw byte sequence of any length with no encoding or content constraints. May contain non-printable bytes and is not required to be NUL-terminated. Suitable for APIs that accept binary/string data and escape or process it internally.
A short string used as an indentation pattern for pretty-printing. Typically composed of spaces or tabs and may be empty; repeated to indent nested structures.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
import itertools

# This generator targets YAJL generator stubs that request arbitrary byte strings
# via FUZZ_PARAM_STR and occasionally use them as:
#  - json string content for yajl_gen_string
#  - indentString when beautify is enabled (kept short, printable)
# We therefore produce bytes that can serve as:
#  - valid UTF-8 strings (to hit fast paths)
#  - strings containing characters requiring escaping (quotes, backslashes, control chars)
#  - multi-byte UTF-8 (including edge cases)
#  - longer random binary payloads (non-UTF8) to exercise escaping and path variations
# The function returns a single bytes buffer per call, limited to <= 4096 bytes.

_PRINTABLE = [
    *(range(ord('0'), ord('9')+1)),
    *(range(ord('A'), ord('Z')+1)),
    *(range(ord('a'), ord('z')+1)),
    ord(' '), ord('\t')
]

_ESCAPE_TRIGGERS = [ord('"'), ord('\\'), 0x00, 0x01, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0c, 0x0d]

# Some interesting UTF-8 code points (valid)
_UTF8_CODEPOINTS = [
    0x0000,  # NUL (control, will be escaped)
    0x001F,  # unit separator (control range end)
    0x0022,  # double quote
    0x005C,  # backslash
    0x00A9,  # ©
    0x03C0,  # π
    0x20AC,  # €
    0x1F600, # 😀
]

# Some valid multi-byte sequences bordering lengths
def _utf8_encode_cp(cp: int) -> bytes:
    if cp <= 0x7F:
        return bytes([cp])
    elif cp <= 0x7FF:
        return bytes([0xC0 | (cp >> 6), 0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)])
    elif cp <= 0xFFFF:
        return bytes([0xE0 | (cp >> 12), 0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F), 0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)])
    else:
        return bytes([0xF0 | (cp >> 18), 0x80 | ((cp >> 12) & 0x3F), 0x80 | ((cp >> 6) & 0x3F), 0x80 | (cp & 0x3F)])

# Some templates for JSON-like segments (though yajl_gen_string accepts raw bytes, not quoted)
# We include them to create diverse content patterns.
_JSONISH_SEGMENTS = [
    b"true", b"false", b"null",
    b"1234567890", b"-0", b"0", b"-12345678901234567890",
    b"1.2345e+10", b"-9.99E-5",
    b"{\"k\":\"v\"}", b"[1,2,3]",
]

# Produce a small printable indent (when used as indentString)
def _make_indent(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # choices: space, tab, two spaces, mixed small
    options = [b" ", b"    ", b"\t", b"  ", b" . ", b"- "]
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return rng.choice(options)
    # Or a short custom printable sequence (1..8 length)
    ln = rng.randint(1, 8)
    return bytes(rng.choices(_PRINTABLE, k=ln))

# Make a buffer with many escapable characters and valid UTF-8
def _make_escapey_utf8(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    chunks = []
    # Start with some ASCII requiring escaping
    base = [ord('"'), ord('\\')] + [0x00, 0x01, 0x08, 0x09, 0x0a, 0x0c, 0x0d]
    chunks.append(bytes(base))
    # Add some unicode codepoints
    cps = list(_UTF8_CODEPOINTS)
    rng.shuffle(cps)
    for cp in cps:
        chunks.append(_utf8_encode_cp(cp))
    # Pad with printable ASCII
    pad_len = max(0, target_len - sum(len(c) for c in chunks))
    if pad_len > 0:
        chunks.append(bytes(rng.choices(_PRINTABLE, k=pad_len)))
    out = b"".join(chunks)
    return out[:target_len]

# Make a valid UTF-8 string covering various lengths and boundaries
def _make_valid_utf8(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    chunks = []
    # Mix ASCII and multibyte sequences
    while sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < target_len:
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.5:
            ln = min(target_len - sum(len(c) for c in chunks), rng.randint(1, 32))
            chunks.append(bytes(rng.choices(_PRINTABLE, k=ln)))
        else:
            cp = rng.choice(_UTF8_CODEPOINTS + [rng.randint(0x80, 0x7FF), rng.randint(0x800, 0xFFFF), rng.randint(0x10000, 0x10FFFF)])
            chunks.append(_utf8_encode_cp(cp))
    out = b"".join(chunks)
    return out[:target_len]

# Make arbitrary binary (may be non-UTF8) to exercise escaping/raw handling
def _make_binary(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    b = bytearray(target_len)
    # Ensure some escapable bytes present
    for i, v in enumerate(itertools.islice(itertools.cycle(_ESCAPE_TRIGGERS), 0, min(len(_ESCAPE_TRIGGERS), target_len))):
        b[i] = v
    # Fill the rest with random bytes
    for i in range(len(_ESCAPE_TRIGGERS), target_len):
        b[i] = rng.randrange(0, 256)
    return bytes(b)

# Make a compact buffer that includes multiple interesting segments concatenated
def _make_combo(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    chunks = []
    # Start with a short indent candidate so the same buffer is useful for indentString
    chunks.append(_make_indent(rng))
    # Add jsonish segments
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        chunks.append(rng.choice(_JSONISH_SEGMENTS))
    # Add escapey utf8
    chunks.append(_make_escapey_utf8(rng, rng.randint(8, 64)))
    # Add some random printable tail
    tail_len = max(0, target_len - sum(len(c) for c in chunks))
    if tail_len:
        chunks.append(bytes(rng.choices(_PRINTABLE + _ESCAPE_TRIGGERS, k=tail_len)))
    out = b"".join(chunks)
    return out[:target_len]

# Deterministically choose a size profile based on seed
def _choose_size(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Mix of small, medium, and near-limit sizes, capped at 4096
    pick = rng.random()
    if pick < 0.25:
        return rng.randint(0, 16)
    elif pick < 0.6:
        return rng.randint(17, 256)
    elif pick < 0.9:
        return rng.randint(257, 2048)
    else:
        return rng.randint(2049, 4096)

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    size = _choose_size(rng)

    # Choose a strategy
    strategies = [
        _make_valid_utf8,
        _make_escapey_utf8,
        _make_binary,
        _make_combo,
    ]
    strat = rng.choice(strategies)

    # Ensure at least some content for empty-size edge
    if size == 0:
        # return a very short but interesting buffer
        size = rng.randint(1, 8)

    buf = strat(rng, size)

    # Occasionally prepend an indent to serve double-duty for indentString cases
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and len(buf) < 4096:
        ind = _make_indent(rng)
        buf = (ind + buf)[:4096]

    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: whitespace/indent string for YAJL generator config.indentString
# The fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain indentSrc when beautify is enabled.
# Our generator should therefore primarily yield short, printable indent patterns that
# exercise different behaviors: empty, spaces, tabs, mixed whitespace, unicode (UTF-8),
# and edge-length (up to 8 bytes as the stub truncates >8).
#
# The returned bytes buffer will be used by the harness to seed FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# We pack multiple candidate strings separated by NULs so the harness can slice them as needed.
# Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

# Helper: build a set of interesting indent candidates
_DEF_WHITESPACE = [
    "",           # empty -> stub replaces with four spaces
    " ",          # single space
    "  ",         # two spaces
    "    ",       # four spaces (common)
    "\t",         # single tab
    "\t\t",       # double tab
    " \t",        # mixed
    "\t ",        # mixed reversed
    " \t \t",     # mixed with spaces
    "\n",         # newline (still printable-ish, tests escaping)
    "\r",         # carriage return
]

# Some UTF-8 sequences that are valid but not ASCII spaces; to test htmlSafe and escaping paths
_UTF8_SAMPLES = [
    "\u00A0",      # non-breaking space
    "\u2003",      # em space
    "\u2009",      # thin space
    "\u3000",      # ideographic space
]

# Convert unicode escape strings to actual characters
def _decode_unicode_escapes(s: str) -> str:
    try:
        return s.encode('utf-8').decode('unicode_escape')
    except Exception:
        return s

_UTF8_WHITES = [_decode_unicode_escapes(u) for u in _UTF8_SAMPLES]

# Additional mixed candidates up to 8 bytes (stub truncates >8)
def _make_mixed_patterns(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    pool = [' ', '\t', '\n', '\r'] + _UTF8_WHITES
    res = []
    for _ in range(12):
        length = rng.randint(1, 8)
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(length))
        res.append(s)
    # Edge cases: exactly 8 bytes of various kinds
    res.extend([
        ' ' * 8,
        '\t' * 8,
        (' \t' * 4)[:8],
    ])
    return res

# Build a corpus of indent strings emphasizing validity and variety
def _build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    corpus: List[bytes] = []
    # Base set
    for s in _DEF_WHITESPACE:
        corpus.append(s.encode('utf-8'))
    # UTF-8 whitespace variants
    for s in _UTF8_WHITES:
        corpus.append(s.encode('utf-8'))
        corpus.append((s + ' ').encode('utf-8'))
        corpus.append((' ' + s).encode('utf-8'))
    # Mixed patterns
    for s in _make_mixed_patterns(rng):
        b = s.encode('utf-8')
        if len(b) <= 8:
            corpus.append(b)
        else:
            corpus.append(b[:8])
    # Also include some printable non-whitespace small tokens to ensure escaping paths
    extras = [
        '..',       # dots
        '->',       # arrows
        '• ',       # bullet + space
        '— ',       # em dash + space
        '\u00A0 ',  # NBSP + space
    ]
    for e in extras:
        corpus.append(_decode_unicode_escapes(e).encode('utf-8')[:8])
    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[bytes] = []
    for b in corpus:
        if b not in seen:
            seen.add(b)
            uniq.append(b)
    return uniq

# Pack multiple strings into a single buffer. The fuzz harness typically slices buffers for FUZZ_PARAM_STR,
# but to be robust we separate entries by NUL (0x00) which is safe for string slicing strategies.
# We ensure total length <= 4096 bytes.

def _pack_entries(entries: List[bytes], max_size: int, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    rng.shuffle(entries)
    out = bytearray()
    for e in entries:
        if not e:
            # include empty entry explicitly
            part = b"\x00"
        else:
            part = e
        # NUL separator between entries
        needed = len(part) + (1 if out else 0)
        if len(out) + needed > max_size:
            break
        if out:
            out.append(0)
        out.extend(part)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    entries = _build_corpus(rng)
    # Bias selection size to a diverse subset each call
    take = rng.randint(8, min(len(entries), 64))
    subset = rng.sample(entries, take)
    buf = _pack_entries(subset, 4096, rng)
    # Ensure non-empty; fallback to four spaces if somehow empty
    if not buf:
        return b"    "
    return buf
